title: Martin Buber
idiom: traditional Jewish papercut (mizrah / ketubah papercut) — hand-cut symmetry, warm parchment, no CGI
hero_prompt: A traditional Jewish papercut illustration, intricate hand-cut symmetry on warm parchment: two facing abstract forms — evoked as stylized trees-of-life / vessels, NOT human portraits — turned toward one another across a luminous vertical GAP of negative space at the very center, and that between-space gap is the brightest, most charged region of the whole image. Along the base, a single narrow ridge-path threads between two dark drops. Stark cut black silhouette against glowing parchment light behind. Absolutely no Hebrew, no script, no characters of any kind. No letters, numerals, words, labels, inscriptions — purely pictorial.
icon_prompt: Bold high-contrast papercut emblem: two simple facing curved forms with a bright vertical GAP of light held between them — the charged space between. Stark black cut-paper silhouette, glowing center, no fine linework, survives at 24px. No Hebrew, no script. No letters, numerals, words, labels, inscriptions — purely pictorial.
